A university maintains the following database tables:
STUDENT: StudentID, Email, PhoneNumber, Name
COURSE: CourseID, CourseName
ENROLLMENT: StudentID, CourseID, Semester
options: Email and PhoneNumber are candidate keys, StudentID is the primary key, and (StudentID, CourseID, Semester) is a composite primary key in ENROLLMENT

CourseID in ENROLLMENT is a primary key and StudentID in STUDENT is a foreign key
(StudentID, CourseID) is a candidate key in STUDENT and Semester is a foreign key

"At Mumbai International Airport, a software system announces flights ready for boarding. The list of flights is stored in an array. 
Developer A uses a loop that accesses each flight using its index and updates a specific flight status to ""DELAYED"".
Developer B uses another loop that reads each flight directly from the list and tries to update the same status.

However, only one of them sees the change reflected in the final announcements.
options:
Developer A used for loop and Developer B used
for-each loop hence Developer A changes were reflected

Developer A
used for loop and Developer B used for-each loop hence Developer B changes
were reflected

Developer A
used for-each loop and Developer B used for loop hence Developer A changes
were reflected

questions.text:
In a ride-sharing application, a base class Vehicle has a method calculateFare().
Classes Car and Bike override this method with their own fare logic.

A Vehicle reference points to a Car object and calls calculateFare().
Another developer directly creates a Vehicle object and calls the same method.

Which fare calculation will be executed for the Vehicle reference pointing to the Car object?

In a banking application, the Account class has a private variable balance.
Developer A updates the balance using a public method deposit().
Developer B tries to modify the balance directly using account.balance = 5000.

Only one developer’s change is accepted by the system.
options: The balance variable is private and accessible only through public methods

questions.text:
In a food delivery app, an interface PaymentService defines a method processPayment().
Classes GooglePay and Paytm implement this interface.

Why is using an interface beneficial in this scenario?
options: It hides implementation and enforces a contract

questions.text:
In a gaming application, a superclass GameCharacter has a subclass Warrior.
A GameCharacter reference stores a Warrior object.

Developer A accesses only superclass methods.
Developer B casts the reference to Warrior and accesses special attack methods.

Which type of casting is Developer B performing?

In an ATM system, when a user withdraws money
a. The account balance is deducted.
b. Cash is dispensed.

Developer A ensures that both steps succeed or both fail.
Developer B allows the balance to be deducted even if cash is not dispensed due to a power failure.

Which ACID property is ensured by Developer A but violated by Developer B?

In a smart payment system, the development team designs a common type PaymentMethod.
a. Developer A defines PaymentMethod as an interface with methods pay() and refund().
b. Developer B defines PaymentMethod as an abstract class that includes:
    i. an abstract method pay()
   ii. concrete method logTransaction()
   iii. a variable to store transaction count

he system requires:
a. Multiple payment classes to share common behavior
b. Ability to store instance variables
c. Flexibility to add default functionality

Which choice best justifies using an abstract class instead of an interface?
options: Interfaces are slower than abstract classes
Interfaces cannot be implemented by multiple classes
Abstract classes can contain both abstract and concrete methods and instance variables

questions.text: Which SQL statement is used to add a new column email of type VARCHAR(50) to an existing table STUDENT?
options: ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD email VARCHAR(50);
MODIFY TABLE STUDENT ADD email VARCHAR(50);
